why: CLAUDE.md (parallel sessions): a session's report NAMES the premises its work rested on and did not test, especially any a peer also accepted. Convergence on such a premise is logged UNCHECKED, never CONFIRMED, and goes to a different KIND of check. This is that list. It is written from inside the session that holds the premises, which is the weakest possible position to write it from — the list is itself a candidate for the blind region it describes.
the_category_is_not_hypothetical_here: one premise on this list was carried UNCHECKED for the whole design phase, was accepted by both sessions, and turned out FALSE: 'the control's per-set stacks are what today's chain produces from today's members'. It was caught only when a canvas mismatch made it impossible to keep — see persset_baseline_correction.json. Nothing about the way it was held marked it as riskier than the others below.

unchecked_and_load_bearing.premise: starlight preservation is the RIGHT adoption gate for the L1 level choice
unchecked_and_load_bearing.status: UNCHECKED — inherited from the pre-registration and accepted by both sessions without either raising it
unchecked_and_load_bearing.why_it_matters: if preservation is not what should decide per-frame vs on-stack, the whole experiment answers a question nobody needed answered. Every number here is conditional on it.
unchecked_and_load_bearing.what_would_check_it: the owner. It is a judgement about what matters, not a measurement, and no instrument can settle it.

unchecked_and_load_bearing.premise: `--gsplit=11` (G = 11.0 at 50% completeness) is the right detection limit on THIS corpus
unchecked_and_load_bearing.status: UNCHECKED for the retained readings, PARTIALLY checked for the bound
unchecked_and_load_bearing.why_it_matters: it defines which Gaia sources count as unresolved, i.e. the predictor itself. It is INHERITED from the archived july23 identification record and is a hypothesis on aug06.
unchecked_and_load_bearing.what_would_check_it: the research pass swept G = 9 to 14 and showed the catalogue BOUND is insensitive to it; nobody has swept the paired RETAINED readings. Every magnitude bin is kept in every record, so the sweep is offline and cheap.

unchecked_and_load_bearing.premise: the 14x10 lattice is an appropriate scale, and the readings are not an artefact of it
unchecked_and_load_bearing.status: UNCHECKED — inherited from the research pass and never varied by either session
unchecked_and_load_bearing.why_it_matters: cell size ranges 350x359 px on a per-set surface to 525x459 on the union, so the four surfaces are not even read at one angular scale. A scale-dependent result would look exactly like a surface-dependent one.
unchecked_and_load_bearing.what_would_check_it: re-run one surface at 10x7 and 20x14 and compare retained. Cheap — the cached Gaia cells make only the new lattice's cells a fresh query.

unchecked_and_load_bearing.premise: `-nodither` per-frame and `subsky` on-stack are two spellings of ONE setting, so dithering is held fixed across the arms
unchecked_and_load_bearing.status: UNCHECKED — asserted in the pre-registration, not probed in this session
unchecked_and_load_bearing.why_it_matters: if they differ, the arms differ by a second knob and the whole comparison is contaminated. The asymmetry is real (`seqsubsky` dithers unless told not to; `subsky` does not unless asked), which is why the pre-registration names it.
unchecked_and_load_bearing.what_would_check_it: the probe that established the per-frame half — two runs of the on-stack operator, differenced. It was run for `seqsubsky` (sigma 0.4 ADU between default runs, bit-identical with -nodither) and never for `subsky`.

unchecked_and_load_bearing.premise: Gaia DR3 incompleteness in the galactic plane does not act DIFFERENTIALLY between the arms
unchecked_and_load_bearing.status: UNCHECKED — scope limit 4 of the instrument, accepted by both sessions
unchecked_and_load_bearing.why_it_matters: the predictor is a proxy that tracks the true faint-star flux rather than equalling it. Both arms are read on the same cells with the same catalogue, so a common bias cancels in the paired difference; a bias that interacts with the arms would not.
unchecked_and_load_bearing.what_would_check_it: no external anchor exists on this rig. It is a documented gap, not a deferred task.

unchecked_and_load_bearing.premise: `retained` is the right summary statistic for the question
unchecked_and_load_bearing.status: UNCHECKED — inherited, and the session then spent most of its analysis effort on how to READ it rather than on whether to use it
unchecked_and_load_bearing.why_it_matters: it is a ratio whose denominator is a poorly-determined measured slope on two of four surfaces (58-67% SE). The session added the bound, the non-resolution phrasing and the denominator analysis around it, all of which take the statistic as given.

no build-path script changed during the run — `git diff --stat 1f261e7..HEAD -- scripts/` is empty, so the PIPEREV moves are records-only
the control's per-set stacks are NOT today's product — FALSIFIED and corrected mid-flight (persset_baseline_correction.json)

the background step did NOT degrade arm A's plate solutions — 13 members, solve logodds donor vs arm A: set-01 203/203/222/127/137 both ways, set-02 223/134/145/156 vs 222/134/145/156, set-03 194/194/103/128 both ways; 0 solve failures in either arm. the pin held on ALL 13 members, not just the first — 13/13 arm A canvases identical to their donor's, 13/13 builder 'registration PINNED' lines, every product stamped REGPIN=gNN.seq and BKGLIGHT=subsky1-nodither
